statement.p: Let \mbox{curl }\vec F = -x\,\mathit{\vec i}-\,\mathit{\vec j}+5z\,\mathit{\vec k}, let P =(2,4,3), and let C be the circle of radius 0.02 centered at P in the plane x+y+z = 9, oriented clockwise when viewed from the origin.
(a) Find \mbox{curl }\vec F\cdot(\vec i+\vec j+\vec k) at P.
(b) Use your answer to part (a) to estimate \int_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r.

static.solution:
(a) At P, we have \mbox{curl } \vec F = -2\,\mathit{\vec i}-\,\mathit{\vec j}+15\,\mathit{\vec k}, so \mbox{curl }\vec F\cdot(\vec i+\vec j+\vec k) = (-2) + (-1) + (15) = 12.
(b) The definition of the curl tells us that if \vec n is the unit vector normal to the plane containing the circle and pointing away from the origin, then \mbox{curl } \vec F\cdot\vec n\approx \frac{\int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r}{\hbox{Area enclosed by }C}. Since \vec n=(\vec i+\vec j+\vec k)/\sqrt 3, we have \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r\approx (\mbox{curl }\vec F \cdot\vec n)(\mbox{Area of circle}) = \frac{12}{\sqrt 3}\pi(0.02)^2 = 0.00870624.
